neighbours.label: a verb of travel or movement through space, especially moving away (sail away, crawl, drift, glide)
fire: From the cliff we saw the old ferry drift slowly away from the pier.
A heron glides low over the marsh and vanishes behind the reeds.
The wounded soldier was crawling through the mud toward the trench.
We stood on the beach and watched the yacht sail out past the lighthouse.
Clouds of starlings swirl above the field and then fly off to the south.
The caravan wandered across the desert for weeks without water.
A lone balloon floated away over the rooftops of the town.
The hikers trudged up the ridge and disappeared into the mist.
quiet: From the cliff we saw the old ferry tied up at the pier.
A heron stands still in the marsh, waiting beside the reeds.
The wounded soldier was lying in the mud beside the trench.
We sat on the beach and admired the yacht moored by the lighthouse.
Clouds of starlings rest on the wires above the field every evening.
The caravan camped in the desert for weeks near a well.
A lone balloon was tied to the railing outside the town hall.
The hikers rested on the ridge and ate lunch in the mist.

notes: Probe: 'sail away' 0.56, 'far away' 0.39, 'crawling' 0.33, 'flutters' 0.24; 'sleeping' 0.17, plain copula sentence 0.03. Logit effect promotes nearby, distant, foreign, local.
